title: Automated fallback sentinels and threshold-driven circuit breakers for smart routing
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement an automated sentinel system and threshold-driven circuit breakers that trigger model fallback and routing changes when per-region or per-tier health signals exceed configurable thresholds. The goal is to reduce visible 429s and tail latency for customers by proactively routing around degraded capacity and switching to validated fallback model variants before user-facing errors spike. This ticket scopes the control plane and runtime integration for detection, decisioning, and safe rollback behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Control plane exposes configurable sentinel thresholds for 429 rate, p95 latency, and error rate per region/tier
Runtime responds to sentinel triggers within configured reaction window and routes new requests to fallback model variant or alternate region
Circuit breaker state machine persists across runtime restarts and respects cooldown/backoff policies
Automated canary test demonstrates circuit breaker closing/opening over synthetic load with no regression in stable-region latency
Documentation updated with operational runbook, SLO impacts, and how to tune thresholds
tech_notes: Signals: 429-per-minute, p95 latency, 5xx-error-rate, queue-drop-rate, and active-inflight-per-gpu
Decisioning: sliding-window counters with EWMA smoothing, default reaction_window=30s, evaluation_interval=10s
Circuit breaker states: CLOSED -> WARMING -> OPEN -> HALF_OPEN -> CLOSED; warmup allows limited degraded traffic for verification
Fallback model variants: mapping table of primary->compatible variants with quantization and sequence-length compatibility checks
Persistence: store breaker state in etcd with TTL and versioned keys to allow multi-runtime ownership
Telemetry: emit breaker_open/breaker_close events with shard, cause, metric_snapshot for postmortem
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind 'routing-sentinels' flag. Stage 1: control-plane only (dry-run) for 48 hours to collect false-positive stats. Stage 2: enable runtime reaction in ~10% of traffic with canary routing. Stage 3: expand to 50% and run extended load tests. Stage 4: full rollout with ops monitoring and rapid rollback playbook.
test_plan: Unit tests for state transitions and TTL behavior
Integration tests: simulated 429 bursts from a specific region and verify routing change within reaction_window
Chaos test: force node restarts while circuit breaker is OPEN and verify persisted state recovery
Performance test: measure p99 tail latency impact with 10% canary enabled
E2E test: synthetic user flows against fallback model variants to validate semantic parity thresholds
